title: Why I run a home lab and what I actually use it for
description: A look inside my home lab: useful self-hosted services, subscription trade-offs, how the setup connects, and where AI fits alongside everyday tools.

assets.alt: Home-lab overview grouping files and storage, media, home automation, networking and hosting, everyday tools, and AI experiments.
assets.caption: The main jobs in the lab, grouped by purpose rather than network layout. This is a snapshot of configured services and explored work, not a claim of daily use. Home automation reflects reported dashboard work, not a newly verified live setup.

assets.alt: Media workflow from an Overseerr request through Sonarr or Radarr and a configured download client to the library, then Plex and viewing devices.
assets.caption: Overseerr manages the request; Plex serves the library. The middle steps depend on the configured download client and storage. This shows the roles, rather than a map of network connections.

assets.alt: Separate roles around Docker: Coolify builds and deploys projects, Portainer manages containers and stacks, Watchtower updates selected images, and Traefik routes web requests to applications.
assets.caption: These are responsibilities around the containers, not successive stops in a request. A browser request goes through the configured proxy to the application; it doesn't travel through every management tool.
